body:
On Ruby 2.3.0, `#to_time` uses system timezone of `#to_time` is called (this precedes timezone of a receiver object).
On Ruby 2.4.0, will use timezone of a receiver object.

> behave consistently on Ruby 2.3.0 and 2.4.0

means "using system timezone of `#to_time` is called" on both Ruby 2.3.0 and 2.4.0 ?

@yui-knk Yes, use local (system tz). We had to compromise when our only options were local tz or utc. I wish we could have preserved tz of the receiver all along!

This is an unfortunate situation, then, since changing `#to_time` behavior will require a major Rails change (5.0.0) and will need a configuration flag to enable. Plus we'll need to emulate Ruby 2.4 `#to_time` for Date/Time/DateTime on Ruby 2.2 and 2.3, which I'm not sure is possible due to internal API usage.
Ugh, will have a look at this today

🤘

The fix for this appears to be a breaking change for reasons I don't understand.

The simplest reproduction is this:

```
irb(main):001:0> frozen_time = Time.now.freeze
=> 2017-03-09 09:07:41 +0000
irb(main):002:0> Time.now >= frozen_time
RuntimeError: can't modify frozen Time
	from .../vendor/bundle/ruby/2.2.0/gems/activesupport-4.2.8/lib/active_support/core_ext/date_and_time/compatibility.rb:23:in `to_time'
	from .../vendor/bundle/ruby/2.2.0/gems/activesupport-4.2.8/lib/active_support/core_ext/time/calculations.rb:261:in `compare_with_coercion'
	from (irb):2:in `>='
        ...
```
@gshutler yes, we're aware of it - see #28147
